Core plugin implementation: - src/index.ts - JSDoc header explicitly links to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` - `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Provide foundational plugin export and registration` - `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies` - Exports ESLint plugin structures in a standard way: - `const rules: Record = {} as any;` - Populated via dynamic `require("./rules/${name}")` for: - require-story-annotation - require-req-annotation - require-branch-annotation - valid-annotation-format - valid-story-reference - valid-req-reference - prefer-implements-annotation - Flat-config presets: - `configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] }` where `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()` returns a v9 flat-config object `{ plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES } }`. - Default export: `export default { rules, configs, maintenance };` with named `rules`/`configs` exports — standard ESLint plugin pattern. - Dynamic rule-loading error handling: - try/catch around `require("./rules/${name}")`. - On failure logs to stderr via `console.error('[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}')`. - Installs a placeholder `RuleModule` that: - `meta.docs.description: 'Failed to load rule ...'`. - `create(context)` reports a Program-level error explaining rule load failure. - This directly implements REQ-ERROR-HANDLING for plugin load/rule load errors.
TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and configs: - src/index.ts - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` defines severity mapping used by both `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`: - `traceability/require-story-annotation`: "error" - `traceability/require-req-annotation`: "error" - `traceability/require-branch-annotation`: "error" - `traceability/valid-annotation-format`: "warn" - `traceability/valid-story-reference`: "error" - `traceability/valid-req-reference`: "error" - `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation`: "warn" - `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` are arrays of flat-config objects (ESLint v9-style), satisfying ESLint v9 flat config compatibility (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM).

traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements from docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md are implemented and traceably tested.
By acceptance criterion: - Core Functionality: src/index.ts exports a conventional ESLint plugin (default and named exports for rules and configs). tests/plugin-setup.test.ts and tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts verify that rules/configs exist, are objects, and that default export properties match named exports. - Quality Standards: The plugin follows ESLint plugin conventions (CommonJS output, flat-config presets, rule registry) and is implemented in TypeScript with a clear tsconfig. Internal guides (docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md, docs/custom-rules-development-guide.md) outline best practices and development workflow. - Integration with ESLint v9 flat config: The plugin exposes flat-config presets (configs.recommended and configs.strict). eslint.config.js is a flat-config-driven setup using this plugin. CLI integration tests (tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts) run ESLint CLI with this config and plugin rules, showing real ESLint v9 flat-config compatibility. - User Experience: README.md documents installation, configuration, example eslint.config.js usage, available rules, and how to run tests and CLI validations, providing clear setup instructions for end users. - Error Handling: src/index.ts wraps dynamic rule loading in try/catch, logs detailed failures, and installs a placeholder rule that surfaces the load error through ESLint reports. tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts validate both programmatic and CLI error behavior, satisfying REQ-ERROR-HANDLING and the story's error-handling acceptance criterion. - Documentation: README.md plus docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md and docs/custom-rules-development-guide.md document plugin structure, configuration, and development/testing setup. This meets the Documentation acceptance criterion and supports ongoing rule development.
Requirement coverage: - REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE: Implemented in src/index.ts and verified via plugin-setup, plugin-default-export-and-configs, and CLI integration tests. - REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT: Achieved through flat-config presets and a flat eslint.config.js actively used by integration tests. - REQ-RULE-REGISTRY: RULE_NAMES and the dynamic loader produce a complete rules object; tests assert exact rule name set and presence in configs. - REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM: configs.recommended and configs.strict provide named presets with a centralized severity mapping, giving users a configurable system. - REQ-NPM-PACKAGE: package.json, tsconfig.json, and the lib/ output path together define a proper, publishable ESLint plugin package. - REQ-TYPESCRIPT: Source and tests are in TypeScript; tsc-based build and type-check scripts are configured. - REQ-TEST-SETUP: Jest and ESLint RuleTester-based tests exist for rules and plugin/CLI integration; CI scripts reference them. - REQ-ERROR-HANDLING: Fully implemented and directly exercised by unit and CLI tests.
Given this evidence, the story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP is fully implemented and satisfies its definition of done within the scope of the repository.
